extraction.name: MATHVISTA
extraction.description: A benchmark designed to combine challenges from diverse mathematical and visual tasks, consisting of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA).
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
extraction.citeAs: Lu et al., 2024, MATHVISTA: EVALUATING MATHEMATICAL REASONING OF FOUNDATION MODELS IN VISUAL CONTEXTS, ICLR 2024
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected from 28 existing multimodal datasets (9 MathQA and 19 VQA datasets) and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA). For existing datasets, examples were limited to up to 400 per source. For VQA datasets, heuristic rules were used to automatically select math-related examples, followed by manual labeling by three expert annotators. New datasets were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields with a two-step review process.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 28 existing multimodal datasets (9 MathQA and 19 VQA datasets) and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For VQA datasets, heuristic rules were used to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning (e.g., numeric answers or quantity words). Then three expert annotators manually labeled these examples to determine if they involve mathematical reasoning, using majority voting. Each source dataset was limited to 400 examples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA), questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields. A two-step process was used: each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers, achieving 99.2% inter-annotation consistency. Discrepancies were resolved through discussion. For mathematical reasoning categories, expert annotators manually labeled 1,000 examples from seven candidates, achieving 94.1% exact match with automatic annotation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-annotator agreement for mathematical reasoning labeling: Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775. For new datasets, inter-annotation consistency rate of 99.2% (only 6 disagreements out of 736 questions).
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Graduate students in STEM fields for new datasets; expert annotators for mathematical reasoning labeling; Amazon Mechanical Turk workers with high school diploma or higher for human performance baseline.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The test set answer labels will not be publicly released to prevent data contamination. An online evaluation platform will be maintained.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Dataset coverage may have gaps in representation of certain mathematical problems and visuals. Only 85.6% of examples have annotations due to heterogeneity of sources. Annotations lack a unified format and structure. The study focused exclusively on the most recent and prominent models.
